features.summary: The Settings page (7 tabs, settings/lib/tabs.ts:16-24) reads and edits payment gateways, tax rates, currencies with the FX refresh, the 8 storefront policies (flat keys of the settings table, saved through PATCH /admin/storefront/settings), notification templates with a server-rendered preview, the sent-notification log, the merchant webhook log with Retry, and a System tab that shows every other settings key (typed field for imeiRetentionDays, adminAllowlistOnly as a link, unknown keys as read-only JSON). Short tables load whole (_start=0&_end=200), logs page by 25 newest first. Every body is an assumed contract (M10).

endpoints.response: One flat JSON object {key: value} of every non-secret settings row (settings.key -> value jsonb); no wrapper, no paging. Values keep their JSON type or the console drops them silently (settings/lib/policies.ts:81-89, lib/system.ts:62-65): guestCheckout, require3ds, withdrawalWaiver, autoRefundFailed, imeiPrecheck are booleans; refundHoursBeforeDispatch, abandonedMinutes, imeiRetentionDays are JSON integers; adminAllowlistOnly is a boolean (read by the access page, M14). A key never set is absent. Any other key (maintenance, risk rules...) is shown read-only as JSON on the System tab (M174), so secret-bearing keys (tokens, passwords) must be omitted or masked. Also read by customers/components/PrivacyPanel.tsx:22 (imeiRetentionDays) and access/hooks/useRestriction.ts:17 (adminAllowlistOnly).

errors.ui: Policies and System tabs hidden; access page restriction switch disabled with the reason

endpoints.mapConflict: Map row gives no body; the table is key/value. Proposal: flat object of typed values (M174, M14).

endpoints.request: Partial flat object {key: value}, merged (listed keys upserted, others untouched). The console sends one key per call; today only {imeiRetentionDays: integer 0-3650} from the System tab (SystemTab.tsx:26, lib/system.ts:20-30). Allow-list: only keys in a settings registry of the platform module are accepted, each with its validator; today that is only imeiRetentionDays (JSON integer 0-3650, the validator shared with PATCH /admin/storefront/settings). Any other key is 422 VALIDATION_FAILED with errors[].field = the key: that includes unknown keys and the keys owned by stricter routes (B67): adminAllowlistOnly (PUT /admin/access/restriction, lock-out guard), the maintenance key (PUT /admin/system/maintenance), the risk rules key (PUT /admin/risk/rules) and the storefront policy keys other than imeiRetentionDays (PATCH /admin/storefront/settings). A later feature that needs a key editable here adds it to the registry with its validator. Valid keys are upserted, merged and audited; then SettingsReader.invalidate() runs. Writes audit_logs with before/after.
endpoints.response: The whole settings object after the change (same shape as GET). The console invalidates and re-reads GET /admin/settings.

Any other key is a 422 on that key ('This is not a storefront setting.'). A number saves on blur/Enter, a switch at once (M169). businessRules: GET /admin/settings is the read source for policies and for keys owned by other routes: values keep JSON types (booleans, integers), secrets are never returned (System tab shows unknown keys as JSON, M174; lib/system.ts:52-59).

Keys with their own guarded route cannot be written through PATCH /admin/settings: adminAllowlistOnly (PUT /admin/access/restriction refuses enabling when the caller's IP is outside the allowlist, scenario ip-rules step 2), maintenance (PUT /admin/system/maintenance, scenario system-integrity steps 4-8), risk rules (PUT /admin/risk/rules) and storefront policies except imeiRetentionDays (map rows; M14).

Storefront policies and ranges (mock storefrontRoutes.ts:8-14): switches guestCheckout, require3ds, withdrawalWaiver, autoRefundFailed, imeiPrecheck; refundHoursBeforeDispatch 0-72 h, abandonedMinutes 5-1440, imeiRetentionDays 0-3650 days. imeiRetentionDays is writable from both PATCH /admin/storefront/settings and PATCH /admin/settings with the same validation (lib/system.ts:20-30).

require3ds is one value: the storefront policy and the risk rule require3ds must always agree; changing either changes the other (demo 12-state-b2c.js:411-415 setPolicy flips rr6; M168; risk/lib/rules.ts:41-45 sameAsSettings).

Policy effects the server enforces (settings/lib/policies.ts:16-62): guestCheckout off = account required at checkout; require3ds = card sessions demand 3D Secure; withdrawalWaiver = checkout records the waiver consent (consent_records); autoRefundFailed = a supplier-rejected storefront order is refunded by the system (refund requestedBy type system); imeiPrecheck = blacklisted IMEI refused before payment (scenario b2c-paid step 1); refundHoursBeforeDispatch = customer self-cancel window before dispatch; abandonedMinutes = delay of the one recovery email; imeiRetentionDays = IMEIs erased or hashed from orders and imei_checks after that many days.

Gateways: code unique and immutable (used in POST /webhooks/payments/:gateway, M162); the secret is write-only, stored encrypted, shown only as secretHint; maxAmount 0 = no maximum else >= minAmount; holdHours 0-720; a gateway with payments cannot be deleted (409 GATEWAY_IN_USE, turn it off instead) (mock gatewayRoutes.ts:30-71, 145-160).

Currencies: rateToBase = units per 1 USD (M167), > 0; markupPercent 0-10; decimals 0-4; code ^[A-Z]{3}$ unique; USD is the base (rate 1, no markup, no refresh); a manual rate change stamps rateUpdatedAt; isStale = non-base and rateUpdatedAt null or older than 24 h, the same rule as the dashboard fx_stale item (settings/lib/currencies.ts:8-27; dashboard/mocks/attentionStorefront.ts:83-94). Storefront prices use the session's locked fx (scenario b2c-paid step 3).
refresh-fx refreshes all active non-base currencies in one provider call, stamps rateUpdatedAt, reports refreshed/failed/source and writes audit_logs (map tables currencies, audit_logs; M164).

Tax rates: country immutable after create; ratePercent 0-100; validFrom required, validTo null or >= validFrom; no delete (map ops LSCU, M163); the server picks the rate in force for the customer's country at checkout (scenario b2c-paid step 3), so overlapping windows for one country and region must be refused.

Templates: unique per (event, channel, audience, locale) -> 422 on event; email needs a subject; event/channel/audience/locale fixed after create; an inactive template is not sent; preview never sends and leaves unknown {{placeholders}} visible (mock templateRoutes.ts:14-63, 116-125).

Notification log and webhook log are read-only; recipients are masked server-side; a webhook retry is refused for delivered (409 DELIVERY_SUCCEEDED) and otherwise queues a new signed attempt immediately (mock logRoutes.ts:22-42; map EVENT rows outbound-hmac).

Every write in this feature (settings, policies, gateways, currencies, refresh, tax, templates, retry) writes audit_logs with before/after (map PATCH /admin/settings and refresh-fx tables; demo logAudit in 12-state-b2c.js:405-425).

questions.question: GET /admin/settings: are the policy keys named guestCheckout, require3ds, withdrawalWaiver, autoRefundFailed, imeiPrecheck, refundHoursBeforeDispatch, abandonedMinutes, imeiRetentionDays? Does the answer carry the other keys as {key: value} for the System tab?

questions.question: PATCH /admin/storefront/settings: is the body a flat set of policy keys? The map says it also changes payment methods and email templates: should the console send those through it, or through their own CRUD routes?

Gateways change through PATCH /admin/payment-gateways/:id (payments:gateways) and templates through the template CRUD (notifications:*), each with its own permission and audit; the storefront route answers the 8 policies after the change.

questions.question: Gateways: are audience values b2c | b2b | both? Is a zero limit 'no limit'? What does holdHours hold? Can the server send secretHint and volume30d? Is code fixed after creation?
questions.proposedAnswer: audience b2c|b2b|both (payment_gateways.audience split by audience); 0 min or max = no limit; secretHint ('••••' + last 4) and volume30d (captured payments, 30 days) are sent; code is immutable because it names the webhook path /webhooks/payments/:gateway. holdHours meaning: see question 9.

questions.question: Currencies: is rateToBase units of the currency per dollar? Will the list carry isStale? Is settings:update really the permission to read the list? What does refresh-fx answer, and can it refresh one currency?

Reading needs settings:update as the map says. refresh-fx answers {refreshed[], failed[], source}; it refreshes every active non-base currency, no per-currency refresh.

questions.proposedAnswer: Event keys are dot-separated: order.received, order.completed, order.failed, support.reply, checkout.abandoned, payment.failed, deposit.approved, plus any event the server emits. Preview takes optional {subject, body} and always returns format. Templates are plain text with {{placeholders}} (format text); HTML is allowed for email only if the server supports it, and the console renders it sandboxed.

questions.question: Notification log: is recipient sent already masked? Which status values exist? Is event the event key rather than an id?
questions.proposedAnswer: Yes: recipient is masked by the server from recipient_type/recipient_id; statuses queued, sent, failed (failed carries error in the detail); event is the key text.
questions.basis: map notifications columns; M172

questions.question: Webhook deliveries: are endpoint and client joined into each row? Which status values exist? Does the detail carry responseBody and a network error? Does a retry make a new attempt at once, and is it rate limited?
questions.proposedAnswer: Yes, endpoint {id, url} and client {id, name} are joined (null if removed); statuses delivered, pending, failed; the detail carries responseBody (truncated) and error; a retry queues a new signed attempt immediately (status pending, attempt + 1) and is refused for delivered; manual retries of one delivery are limited to one per minute (429 with Retry-After).
questions.basis: map webhook_deliveries + webhook_endpoints + clients; POST /admin/webhook-deliveries/:id/retry; M173; mock logRoutes.ts:22-42

questions.question: Tax rates: should two rates for one country be refused when their dates overlap? Which taxType values exist?
questions.proposedAnswer: Yes: refuse an overlapping validFrom-validTo window for the same country and region (422 on validFrom), because the server must pick exactly one rate per order. taxType values: vat, gst, sales_tax, none.
questions.basis: map tax_rates (valid_from, valid_to, oss_scheme); scenario b2c-paid step 3; settings/lib/tax.ts:28-34; M163

questions.question: What does payment_gateways.hold_hours do (the form hint says 'Manual review time', the card 'Held for N hours')?
questions.proposedAnswer: Proposed: hours a payment through this gateway stays pending for manual review before the wallet is credited (0 = credit when confirmed); after that time the pending deposit becomes more urgent on the dashboard, nothing is credited or cancelled automatically.
questions.basis: map payment_gateways.hold_hours (no semantics given); GatewayFields.tsx:104; GatewayCard.tsx:61

businessRules: Held = a paid storefront order whose risk assessment decided review and nobody reviewed it yet; held orders never reach the supplier until approved (map GET /admin/risk/queue; scenario b2c-paid steps 3, 6-7; risk/mocks/store.ts:20-22).

Approve and refund only act on a held order: anything else is 409 NOT_HELD; the decision stamps reviewed_by, reviewed_at, outcome (approved|refunded) and writes order_events and audit_logs (mock queue.ts:30-50; demo 12-state-b2c.js:296-313; map approve tables orders, risk_assessments, order_events).

Refund of a held order: order rejected, supplier never contacted, refunds row created, ledger b2c_refund posted (Dr customer_funds net, Dr vat_payable VAT, Cr gateway_clearing gross) in one transaction, gateway refund queued with an idempotency key (map moneyEvent b2c_refund; scenario b2c-refund steps 4-6; src/mocks/ordersActions.ts:77-111).
Blocking on refund adds blocklist entries only (email, IMEI), skipping duplicates silently; customers.status is not changed (map route tables; M106, M73).

Rules: reviewThreshold < blockThreshold always (map PUT /admin/risk/rules); score >= blockThreshold blocks (payment cancelled), >= reviewThreshold holds for review; maxOrdersPerEmail per 24 h; reviewFirstOrderAbove in whole USD for a new customer's first order; reviewIpCountryMismatch adds 25 points; blockDisposableEmail; blockBlacklistedImei at checkout (risk/lib/rules.ts:16-54). Rules are stored in settings and every change is audited (demo 12-state-b2c.js setRule).
IMEI retention: after imeiRetentionDays the IMEI is erased or hashed (map GET /admin/imei-checks description); the list keeps sending a non-null masked or hashed text and matching uses imei_hash.
Permissions: page and reads risk:read; approve/refund risk:decide; blocklist add risk:create, remove risk:delete; rules PUT needs the whole area risk:* (risk/lib/permissions.ts:4-13; M111).

businessRules: Refund states: requested -> completed (approve) or rejected (decline); failed -> completed (retry). Only requested can be approved or declined (409 REFUND_NOT_PENDING); only failed can be retried (409 REFUND_NOT_FAILED) (mock refundRoutes.ts:41-90; demo 12-state-b2c.js:243-263).

Refundable amount = payment amount minus completed refunds on the same payment; approve refuses 0 or more than that with 422 on amount (mock refundRoutes.ts:49-67; demo refundable 12-state-b2c.js:294). Storefront orders are refunded here; completed merchant orders through POST /admin/orders/:id/refund (M25).

Ledger on approval, once per refund (idempotency key per refund, refunds.ledger_tx_id): delivered order -> Dr revenue + Dr vat_payable, Cr gateway_clearing; undelivered -> Dr customer_funds + Dr vat_payable, Cr gateway_clearing and the order is cancelled (map approve 'reversed according to whether the order was delivered'; moneyEvent b2c_refund; scenario b2c-refund step 4). Supplier cost is never recovered once delivered. VAT goes back in proportion (M118). Retry posts nothing.

Gateway flow: outbox job refunds.process sends the refund with an idempotency key; webhook refund.succeeded sets completed and gateway_refund_id; a failure sets failed with the gateway's note (scenario b2c-refund steps 5-7). Crypto payments are refunded by hand: method manual, completed at once, no gateway call (demo 12-state-b2c.js:234-241).
Payment status follows refunds and disputes: partial_refund while refunded total < paid, refunded when equal, chargeback after a lost dispute (mock refundActions.ts:46, disputeActions.ts:28).
Decline needs a reason of at least a sentence, emails it to the customer and writes the order timeline (map decline tables refunds, notifications; mock refundRoutes.ts:71-78).

Dispute states: needs_response -> under_review (evidence) or lost (accept); won/lost also arrive by POST /webhooks/disputes/:gateway. Evidence only before evidence_due_at (409 EVIDENCE_DEADLINE_PASSED); answering a dispute not in needs_response is 409 DISPUTE_NOT_OPEN (mock disputeRoutes.ts:54-83).

A lost dispute posts exactly one chargeback transaction, Dr chargeback_loss amount + fee, Cr gateway_clearing (moneyEvent b2c_chargeback), whether it comes from accept or from the webhook (disputes.ledger_tx_id guards double posting). Accept does not block the customer (M115; map accept tables).

endpoints.response: One object, every section from one snapshot. generatedAt = server time. stats.current = orders created in the rolling window [now - days x 24 h, now] within scope: revenue = sum total_price (excl. VAT) of completed ones, profit = revenue - total_cost (before gateway fees), orders = count of all statuses, successRate = completed/(completed+rejected) x 100 (JSON number, null when none), medianTurnaroundSeconds = median of completed_at - created_at (null when none); previous = the same-length window before, null when it has no order (mocks/stats.ts:5-37). attention = every item, ranked critical > high > medium > low (stable), facts only, opaque string ids (rules in businessRules). queues = 4 rows imei, server, remote, file: open (pending|processing), review (orders whose derived queue, decision 025, is manual (status pending + dispatch_state manual), needs_attention (dispatch_state needs_attention), review (dispatch_state held, the risk hold) or verification (status completed + verification_status requested); dispatch_state 'operator' (accepted by staff) has queue null, is not review, counts in open and can be past SLA), pastSla (open and older than the service SLA, review orders included: the age-only B92 predicate shared with GET /admin/orders?pastSla=true, orders_past_sla, navCounts.orders.pastSla and GET /admin/system/orders-health; a service with a null or 0 SLA is never past SLA), oldestCreatedAt or null. suppliers = every supplier incl. disabled: enabled (status active), health up|degraded|down|unknown mapped from the supplier's latest service_checks row (component 'supplier', supplier_id): ok→up, degraded→degraded, down→down, and unknown or no check yet→unknown (an idle supplier: never shown as healthy, never as a fault; the console shows "No recent calls", B180; a contract test covers the mappings), successRate1h (0-100) or null, p50Ms or null, balance (USD: balance × suppliers.credit_rate), lowBalance (judged in the supplier's own units: balance < low_balance_alert; runwayDays compares USD against USD). ordersByType.daily = 30 UTC days oldest first {date 'YYYY-MM-DD', imei, server, remote, file} of orders created; monthly = 12 UTC months {month 'YYYY-MM', ...} oldest first, null only for a scope with no history. revenueByChannel (scope=all only, else null) = 30 UTC days of completed revenue excl. VAT by completed_at {date, b2b, b2c} plus totals last7Days and last30Days. storefront (null for b2b) = always the last 30 days: funnel {visitorsEstimated, imeiChecks, checkoutsStarted (paid + abandoned sessions), paid, delivered}, averageOrder (paid incl. VAT over non-rejected orders created in the window {id, name, country, orders, spend}. navCounts = whole console whatever the scope: orders {open, pastSla}, finance {pendingDeposits}, merchants {pendingApproval}, support {open, late}, refunds {open = requested + failed refunds + needs_response disputes, disputesDueSoon = needs_response due within 3 days}, risk {held}. Units: money 4-dp strings, rates JSON numbers 0-100, durations named in the field. Money: every money field is in USD (base currency) as a 4-dp string. orders amounts (unit/total price, cost, tax_amount) are already stored in USD (orders.currency is only the buyer's display currency) and need no conversion. payments, refunds and disputes amounts are in their own currency: a row tied to a checkout session (B2C) converts at the rate locked there (amount ÷ checkout_sessions.fx_rate, units per 1 USD, as the ledger does, B111); a row with no locked rate (for example a pending B2B deposit in EUR) converts at the current currencies.rate_to_base; a USD row is taken as is. Convert per row in SQL numeric and round the sum once, half-up to 4 dp (decision 011). crossCutting: Bodiless action POSTs: risk approve, refresh-fx and webhook retry send no body and no Content-Type (risk/api/queue.ts:23, settings/api/currencies.ts:57, settings/api/webhooks.ts:44; the client sets Content-Type only when a body exists, src/lib/api/client.ts:61-68), while refunds retry, dispute accept and template preview send '{}' as JSON (refunds/api/refunds.ts:69, refunds/api/disputes.ts:58, settings/api/templates.ts:80-83). Action body schemas must be optional and accept both forms.

Settings values keep their JSON types: booleans as true/false and counts as JSON integers; the console silently drops a value of another type (settings/lib/policies.ts:81-89, settings/lib/system.ts:62-65), so jsonb setting values must never be stringified.

Field-error names are matched loosely here: a policy message by key or any 'prefix.key' (settings/lib/policies.ts:101-109); a rule message by id, 'rules.<id>.value' or 'rules.<index>.value' (risk/lib/rules.ts:129-137); a bare 409 ALREADY_BLOCKED without errors[] lands on the value field (risk/components/AddBlockDialog.tsx:30, src/components/ui/dialogSubmit.ts:58-66), so keep errors[] empty on that 409.

Decimal inputs on settings forms are typed text with any number of decimals ('2.9', '0.30', '0.79'; settings/lib/decimal.ts:14-17, settings/components/GatewayDialog.tsx:34-53, CurrencyDialog.tsx:44-52, TaxRateDialog.tsx:35-47); edits are compared by trimmed text (decimal.ts:19-22). Accept 0-8 decimals and answer normalised strings (4 dp for money and percents, mock settings/mocks/http.ts:66-69).

Ratios differ by field: JSON numbers 0-100 for dashboard rates and risk heldShare (dashboard/types/index.ts:7-10, risk/types/index.ts:70-71); percent decimal strings, not padded, for report feeRate and refundedPercentOfSales (refunds/types/index.ts:145-156; mock refunds/mocks/reportRoutes.ts:32,52); risk rule values are whole JSON numbers, including a USD amount (risk/types/index.ts:165-172).

Polling load: the sidebar polls GET /admin/dashboard?scope=all&days=7 every 60 s on every page (dashboard/hooks/useDashboardNavCounts.ts:16-20, dashboard/hooks/useDashboard.ts:8,14); the Risk page polls the queue and four IMEI counts every 30 s (risk/hooks/keys.ts:31, risk/hooks/useImeiChecks.ts:57-66); the Refunds page five figure calls and its lists every 30 s (refunds/hooks/useRefundFigures.ts:20-67, refunds/hooks/keys.ts:18). Cache the dashboard per (scope, days) about 15 s and back filtered counts with indexes.

GET /admin/queues is a top-level browser navigation to the API origin (dashboard/api/dashboard.ts:37-39, src/lib/api/client.ts:33-40): Bull Board must authenticate by the staff session cookie (sent on cross-subdomain top-level GETs, SameSite=Lax), check queues:read, need no CSRF header, and bypass the JSON, problem+json and CORS layers.

Calendar dates travel as midnight-UTC instants: tax validFrom/validTo are sent as 'YYYY-MM-DDT00:00:00.000Z' and shown as UTC days (settings/lib/tax.ts:70-85); dashboard chart buckets are UTC 'YYYY-MM-DD' and 'YYYY-MM' strings (dashboard/types/index.ts:7-10, dashboard/mocks/util.ts:1-27). Store tax dates as date and answer midnight UTC.

Most reads in these features need joins beyond the map's table lists (held-order customer and payment, IMEI check customer/supplier/order, blocklist createdBy, refund order/payment/ledger split, dispute customer, webhook endpoint/client, masked notification recipient, gateway volume30d, template sentLast30Days, dashboard sections): risk/types/index.ts:34-63, refunds/types/index.ts:53-75, settings/types/webhooks.ts:12-17, settings/types/gateways.ts:14-19, dashboard/types/index.ts:171-182. Module boundaries must allow cross-module read models.

Ids: RF-, DP-, SF- prefixes are added by the console only (refunds/lib/labels.ts:8-15, M32); dashboard attention item ids are opaque strings (dashboard/types/index.ts:48); every other id is a JSON number. :id in POST /admin/risk/orders/:id/* is the order id (risk/api/queue.ts:22-33).
